what_its_for: Atorvastatin is used to lower bad cholesterol (LDL) and fats (triglycerides) in your blood, while raising good cholesterol (HDL). It helps reduce your risk of heart attack, stroke, and other heart and blood vessel problems. It works best when combined with a heart-healthy diet and regular exercise.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Unlike some other cholesterol medicines, atorvastatin can be taken at any time of day — morning or evening both work fine.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 10 to 20 mg once daily. Your doctor may increase your dose over time, up to a maximum of 80 mg per day, depending on how your cholesterol responds. Always follow your doctor's instructions and do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store atorvastatin at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired tablets safely — ask your pharmacist about medication take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of grapefruit juice (more than 1 quart per day), as it can increase the amount of atorvastatin in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Limit alcohol, as it can increase the risk of liver problems. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about all medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, especially blood thinners, antifungals, certain antibiotics, or other cholesterol medicines, as they can interact with atorvastatin.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, weakness, or cramps (especially with fever or dark-colored urine, which could be a sign of a serious muscle problem called rhabdomyolysis); yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain (possible signs of liver problems); unusual tiredness or loss of appetite; memory problems or confusion; or signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: You may start to see changes in your cholesterol levels within 2 to 4 weeks of starting atorvastatin. Your doctor will check your cholesterol with a blood test after about 4 to 12 weeks to see how well the medicine is working. It is important to keep taking it even if you feel fine — high cholesterol usually has no symptoms, but the medicine is still protecting your heart.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do NOT take atorvastatin if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It can harm an unborn baby or a nursing infant. Use effective birth control while taking this medicine and tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Children: Atorvastatin may be prescribed for children aged 10 and older with certain inherited cholesterol conditions — always follow the pediatrician's instructions. Older adults (65+): This medicine can be used in older adults, but they may be more sensitive to muscle-related side effects. Report any muscle pain or weakness to your doctor promptly. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have liver disease, as atorvastatin may not be safe for you. Dose adjustments may be needed for some patients.
